what: STAG Industrial is a REIT that owns single-tenant industrial buildings. Unlike rivals who concentrate on the largest logistics hubs, it buys warehouses and light manufacturing properties in secondary markets across the United States.
customers: Manufacturers, distributors and logistics operators who need a single building rather than space in a multi-tenant facility, in cities where fewer institutional landlords compete.
money: Leases on single-tenant industrial buildings, typically with tenants paying operating costs and annual rent increases.
moat: Buying in secondary markets means less competition from large institutions, so STAG acquires at higher yields. Single-tenant buildings are simple to manage, and once a tenant has fitted out a warehouse it usually renews rather than move its racking and equipment.
risks: Debt of about $3.3B against only $14.9M of cash means the company depends on capital markets for both refinancing and growth.
Secondary markets have fewer alternative tenants, so re-letting an empty single-tenant building can take a long time.
Growth comes from buying properties, and acquisition yields have narrowed as more capital chases industrial real estate.
The shares trade at about 25.6 times earnings and 15.9 times EV/EBITDA.
National warehouse oversupply has slowed rent growth across the sector.
opportunities: Revenue has grown every year shown, from $562.2M in 2021 to $845.2M in 2025.
Leases signed years ago sit below current market rents, so renewals raise income without new capital.
Free cash flow of $306.1M supports a monthly dividend, which is unusual among REITs and attracts income investors.
Twelve analysts average a $41.25 target, about 14% above the current price.
watch: Re-leasing spreads and retention. Secondary-market single-tenant buildings live or die on whether tenants renew, so the retention rate alongside the rent change is the clearest health check.
